method: Three rounds. Round 1 (10-photo run): the named-text cross-check compared alt_text against a photo's stored visible_text with no stoplist. A read-only frequency query against production photo_metadata.visible_text (22,442 rows, 11,512 distinct values) showed the highest-frequency single-word values are generic vocabulary alt_text is expected to use (volleyball 1,025x, home 320x, team 220x, blue 88x, court 48x, dive 44x), and several MULTI-word entries are entirely generic too (beach volleyball 42x, high school 65x, senior night 45x, game ball 33x, track & field 46x). Added NAMED_TEXT_STOPWORDS; an entry (single- or multi-word) is skipped only when every one of its words is in that stoplist, so a genuinely identifying word anywhere in the phrase (a school/team name, a surname) still triggers the reject. Round 2: re-ran the real, fixed extractOne against the same 10 DWdCET (Milliken at North Central) photos used for the captions receipt, capturing each photo's own visible_text and running inspectAltText against it — 10/10 alt-text-contract clean. Read all 10 source images directly and checked each alt_text against the frame: 10/10 correctly avoid every jersey number, name, and piece of printed text. Note on this round's evidence value: none of the 10 photos' own real visible_text words (CARDINALS, MILLIKIN, PEPSI, GENEVA, NORTH-CENTRAL, VOLLEYBALL, SPORTS) happened to also appear inside that same photo's alt_text, so this round did not exercise the stoplist logic itself (an unfixed version would have scored identically) — the stoplist fix's evidence is the frequency query plus the unit tests (alt-text-contract.test.ts), not this rerun. 3 of 10 (DSC09432, 09435, 09437) mislabel the on-court action verb (serve vs. set vs. spike) — a pre-existing vision-model action-classification limitation shared with the caption on the same photos, not specific to alt_text and not fixed here. Round 3: after the initial single-word-only stoplist filter shipped, found it did not cover the measured multi-word all-generic entries (beach volleyball etc.); fixed to split each entry into words and skip only when every word is in the stoplist; added regression tests for both the single- and multi-word cases, including a phrase with one genuinely identifying word (aurora central catholic) which is correctly NOT skipped. Also found and fixed, this session: scripts/ingest-album.ts's photo_metadata upsert never wrote alt_text at all (extractOne returned it, nothing persisted it) — confirmed by reading the upsert payload; now included.
scope: production visible_text frequency query (22,442 rows), single- and multi-word stoplist fix grounded in it
